properties.entry: shows the components in the Bootstrap look beside their own, and in a look made of both

A theme gives the components their colors, a look the CSS classes of their parts. Every element a component draws is a part (LookPart): a dialog's header, a table's header, a dropdown's option... The Antilia look draws them with their own style sheets; the Bootstrap look gives each part Bootstrap's classes as well, such as btn btn-primary btn-sm for a button, modal-header for the header of a dialog, table for a data table or dropdown-item for an option. Only Bootstrap's style sheet is on the page, never its script: what the components do stays their own.

A look can be made of others, an aspect from each: what the parts are, their colors, their sizes and their states. Look.BOOTSTRAP.with(LookAspect.COLOR, Look.ANTILIA).with(LookAspect.SIZE, Look.ANTILIA) gives the parts Bootstrap's classes with the colors and the sizes of the Antilia look, as the third column shows.

The colors stay the theme's. The Bootstrap themes take them from the custom properties of the Bootstrap on the page, so a theme of Bootswatch or of your own colors the components too; any other theme gives its colors to Bootstrap's components and custom properties, so the page's own Bootstrap markup inside it matches the components.

In Wicket a ThemeBehavior puts the look on a component and everything inside it, as the attribute data-antilia-look, which the scripts of the components read too. The look of the session, Looks.setSessionLook or the model Looks.sessionLook(), is that of every page once chosen on one, as with the Look of the top bar. React has LookProvider and Svelte setLook.

The same components in the looks of ui-components, in the theme chosen in the top bar.
